claims.excerpt: Why the 1906 Earthquake Has Different Magnitude Estimates
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: The verified source reports a surface-wave magnitude of 7.7 and a moment magnitude of 7.9; the synthesis says different methods of estimating earthquake size can disagree.
claims.synthesisStatement: Different methods of estimating earthquake size can disagree.
claims.narrativeStatement: Different methods of estimating earthquake size can disagree.
claims.explanation: The title accurately signals that the source reports differing estimates.

claims.excerpt: One team studied seismic recordings from 96 observatories, then digitized and modeled usable data from 12.
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: The verified source says recordings came from 96 observatories and 12 stations had records suitable for digitization and modeling.
claims.synthesisStatement: One team studied seismic recordings from 96 observatories and digitized and modeled usable data from 12.
claims.narrativeStatement: One team studied seismic recordings from 96 observatories and digitized and modeled usable data from 12.
claims.explanation: The counts and description of the usable records match the evidence.

claims.excerpt: Its analysis suggested a surface-wave magnitude of 7.7 for the 1906 earthquake.

claims.narrativeStatement: That seismic analysis suggested a surface-wave magnitude of 7.7.
claims.explanation: The estimate and its surface-wave scale are accurately stated.

claims.excerpt: A USGS team took a different approach, re-evaluating geodetic measurements made before and after the earthquake.
claims.label: F0
claims.sourceEvidence: The verified source says USGS re-evaluated geodetic measurements from before and after the event.
claims.synthesisStatement: A USGS team instead re-evaluated geodetic measurements made before and after the earthquake.
claims.narrativeStatement: A USGS team instead re-evaluated geodetic measurements made before and after the earthquake.
claims.explanation: The team, method, and timing match the evidence; “different approach” is supported by the contrast with the seismic analysis.

claims.excerpt: Those measurements captured ground deformation through angles and distances between benchmarks, producing an estimate of 7.9.
claims.label: F2
claims.sourceEvidence: The verified source says deformation was assessed using benchmark distances and angles, and that slip models suggested moment magnitude 7.9.
claims.synthesisStatement: The geodetic approach used ground deformation reflected in angles and distances between benchmarks and gave an estimate of 7.9; it does not specify the magnitude scale.
claims.narrativeStatement: The geodetic approach used ground deformation reflected in angles and distances between benchmarks and gave an estimate of 7.9.
claims.explanation: The body follows the synthesis but omits the verified source's material qualification that 7.9 is moment magnitude. It also compresses the role of slip models into “producing an estimate.”
